changeability.rationale: Cross-cutting values (sprites, names, dashes, base URL, caching) are funneled through single helpers, so most fixes are one-line; the exception is team state, which is re-implemented rather than shared, and the card-construction duplication below means a fix needing the Pokémon record would touch three sites.

app/src/lib/api.ts:1 — the server-only fetch/cache layer is cleanly separated from the pure helpers in format.ts and from components

app/src/components/ui.tsx:41 — Section/CardList/TypeBadge/MoveTable stretch across all pages without flag creep

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions are mostly right-sized and an Items section would reuse find/englishName/Section/CardList/orDash/pageTitle wholesale; the deduction is card assembly being copy-pasted in three places and the column config being duplicated inside MoveTable.

findings.issue: Card construction (id/name/label/sprite assembly) is copy-pasted in three places: cardsForPokemon (data.ts:81), homePage (data.ts:139) and teamPage (data.ts:397); the default-variety lookup is likewise duplicated at data.ts:216 and data.ts:385.
findings.suggestion: Extract a cardForSpecies(id, name, extra?) helper plus a shared defaultVariety(species) helper, and have homePage and teamPage go through them; that makes the sprite/species fix and any future card change a one-line edit.

findings.issue: Team state (read/writeTeamCookie, signal mirroring via useTask$, add/remove logic) is implemented independently in the Pokémon page and again in app/src/routes/team/index.tsx:26-40, so a change to team semantics (size, storage, dedup) lands in two routes.
findings.suggestion: Move it into a shared useTeam() composable (context provider or hook) in src/lib, and have both routes consume it.

findings.issue: The shared Card interface and PokemonCard carry a hidden flag plus markup (components/ui.tsx:28) and styling (global.css:256) that exist only for the abilities feature, so removing abilities leaves dead plumbing.
findings.suggestion: Keep the generic card pure and render the 'Hidden ability' note from the ability page (a slot or an extra node prop), or accept the flag but co-locate its markup/CSS with the feature.

findings.issue: All page builders (home, pokemon, move, ability, types, type, team) live in one 400-line module; every new page grows the same file and the section dividers are the only navigation.
findings.suggestion: Split into per-feature modules (lib/pages/pokemon.ts, lib/pages/move.ts, …) or colocate each builder next to its route; the pokemon/ability/move loaders share a find+isValidName+404 shape that could also be factored.

findings.issue: The column list is declared twice: COLUMNS at move-table.tsx:11-19 and the hard-coded <td> sequence at move-table.tsx:63-73, so adding or reordering a column requires two edits.
findings.suggestion: Derive the body cells from the same COLUMNS config (or a cell renderer map keyed by column key).

findings.issue: team.ts mixes browser cookie persistence with pure coverage math, and the server-side data layer imports it (data.ts:6), blurring the server/shared boundary.
findings.suggestion: Split coverage math (coverageRows/TypeRelations) into lib/coverage.ts and keep cookie helpers in lib/team.ts.

findings.issue: API responses are consumed as any throughout (data.ts:216, 223, 233, 277, 301, 319), so a change to the API shape produces no compiler signal when editing these builders.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API records used (Species, Pokemon, Move, …) so refactors of these functions are type-checked.

findings.issue: The team page inlines its own <ul class="card-grid"> instead of reusing CardList, creating a second card-list renderer to keep in sync with CSS and semantics.
findings.suggestion: Give CardList an optional per-item slot (or children render) so the remove button can be added without duplicating the list markup.

summary: A well-organized Qwik City app on the current stable line: one route directory per page, a clean server-only API/cache seam in lib/api.ts, and genuinely reusable Section/CardList/MoveTable abstractions, so most cross-cutting fixes (sprites, names, dashes, base URL) land in one helper. The weaknesses are confined: card assembly is copy-pasted in three places in lib/data.ts, team state is re-implemented in two routes, and the abilities feature leaks a flag and markup into the shared Card component. Those are cheap to fix now and would keep the code pleasant to extend for years.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: The route directory deletes cleanly and the Pokémon page's Abilities section is an obvious grep hit, but abilityPage (data.ts:315), the Card.hidden flag (data.ts:17), the card-note markup (ui.tsx:28) and its CSS (global.css:256) all become dead code that a careless removal would leave behind.

scenarios.change: Fix the card sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: As written the fix is one line: spriteUrl() at data.ts:23 is the only place a card sprite is computed and all three card lists use it. The caveat is that if the fix requires reading the Pokémon record (sprites.front_default) instead of deriving from the ID, card assembly is duplicated at data.ts:81, 139 and 397 and would need three edits — the existing default-variety logic at data.ts:216/385 is the natural seam to factor out.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Two edits in one file: sort in cardsForPokemon (covers move, ability and type pages) and sort before the pagination slice in homePage (data.ts:130-139), since home is server-paginated and sorting in CardList would break across-page ordering. The team page must stay in insertion order per the feature spec, which the current structure makes natural because it doesn't use CardList.

scenarios.notes: High reuse: find/get, isValidName, englishName, shortEffect/latestFlavorText, orDash, pageTitle, Section, TypeBadge, CardList, NotFound and the status(404)+resolveValue head pattern all apply directly. What you copy is the ~35-line route file and a new itemPage() builder in the already-400-line data.ts — a new lib module or colocation would make it a pure add.
